newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Philippines' Ramos denies stopping maid film.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos denies stopping maid film.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday denied he had stopped the screening of a film about a Filipina maid who escaped execution in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), saying the issue was under review.
"To tell you frankly, it is not the president that bans films in the Philippines," Ramos told a news conference at the end of a two-day visit to Bahrain.
"There are a series of authorities that first review the films that are produced in the Philippines. This is not censorship, they just review," he added.
Officials in Manila earlier on Tuesday said the film's showing was stopped after the UAE said it would harm ties.
Ramos ordered state censors to defer the film's scheduled public screening on Wednesday ... "due to anticipated extremely negative impact on Philippines-UAE relations", the presidential palace said.
"The proposed release of the movie has been deferred. The movie ... would be subject to further review," Ramos said.
Showing the film "Sarah Balabagan Story" would also endanger negotiations to save the life of another Filipino jailed in the UAE for killing an Indian national, Ramos said.
A Manila court also issued a temporary restraining order preventing the film's showing after a local Moslem group protested that some scenes were offensive to Islam.
The movie is based on the story of the young Balabagan who was sentenced to death by a UAE court for stabbing to death her Arab employer who she had accused of trying to rape her in 1994.
After UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan intervened, the sentence on Balabagan was reduced to one year in jail and 100 lashes.
The case drew wide international publicity that angered UAE officials.

Balabagan received a heroine's welcome in Manila when she returned last year and has become a symbol of the four million Filipinos working overseas. They include tens of thousands of housemaids and nightclub dancers.
The Philippine Foreign Office said the UAE had expressed deep concern about the film.
A Manila Foreign Office statement cited the role played by the UAE president in saving Balabagan's life.

It added: "The UAE is now asking the Philippine government to do a similar favour from the President (Ramos), to exert influence to stop the showing of the film which they believe will cause them embarrassment."
The showing of the movie could prejudice the welfare of about 80,000 Filipinos working in the UAE, including several facing criminal charges in UAE courts, it added.
